Evaluating the Business Impact of Artificial Intelligence Adoption Across the Quality Engineering Lifecycle¶

Interim Analytical Notebook
Satish Venugopal
Walsh College
QM640: Data Analytics Capstone
Mentor: Ms. Sanhita Karmakar

Research Questions¶

  1. RQ1: Does AI adoption significantly improve productivity across Quality Engineering activities?
  2. RQ2: Does AI-generated business value differ across Quality Engineering lifecycle phases?
  3. RQ3: Which project characteristics and Quality Engineering factors influence productivity improvement?
  4. RQ4: Can machine-learning models predict productivity improvement and identify priority AI-adoption areas?

The analysis uses a 95% confidence level and a significance threshold of α = .05. Predictive results are interpreted as directional decision support rather than causal evidence or an autonomous investment recommendation.

def locate_repository_root():
    current = Path.cwd().resolve()
    candidates = [current, current.parent, current.parent.parent]
    for candidate in candidates:
        if (candidate / "data" / "raw" / "EQEPD_Dataset_v5.xlsx").exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "Repository root was not found. Run the notebook from the repository "
        "root or from the notebooks folder."
    )

REPO_ROOT = locate_repository_root()

PROCESSED_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "processed"

def save_figure(filename):

    plt.show()
    plt.close()
    print(f"Saved: {output_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}")

print(f"Repository root: {REPO_ROOT}")

clean_data = data.drop_duplicates().copy()

application_map = {

    "enterprise data platform": "Enterprise Data Platform",
}

team_map = {
    "legacy support qa": "Legacy Support QA",
    "crm platform qa": "CRM Platform QA",
    "crm qa": "CRM Platform QA",
    "billing & payments qa": "Billing & Payments QA",
    "billing-payments qa": "Billing & Payments QA",
    "billing qa": "Billing & Payments QA",
    "eip-qa": "EIP-QA",
    "erp operations qa": "ERP Operations QA",
    "mobile & web qe": "Mobile & Web QE",
    "mobile/web qe": "Mobile & Web QE",
    "api & middleware qa": "API & Middleware QA",
    "data platform qa": "Data Platform QA",
}

complexity_map = {
    "high": "High", "h": "High",
    "medium": "Medium", "med": "Medium",
    "low": "Low", "l": "Low",
}

clean_data["Application_Name"] = (
    clean_data["Application_Name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.casefold().map(application_map)
)
clean_data["Team_Name"] = (
    clean_data["Team_Name"].astype(str).str.strip().str.casefold().map(team_map)
)
clean_data["Complexity"] = (
    clean_data["Complexity"].astype(str).str.strip().str.casefold().map(complexity_map)
)

ai_columns = [
    column for column in clean_data.columns
    if column.startswith("AI Usage Testing Phase")
]

def normalise_ai_label(value):
    label = str(value).strip().casefold()
    if label in {"yes", "y"}:
        return "Yes"
    if label in {"no", "n"}:
        return "No"
    return np.nan

for column in ai_columns:
    clean_data[column] = clean_data[column].map(normalise_ai_label)

clean_data["Year"] = clean_data["Sprint #"].str.extract(r"(\d{4})").astype(int)
clean_data["Sprint_Number"] = clean_data["Sprint #"].str.extract(r"S(\d+)").astype(int)

context_imputation = {}
for column in ["User story count", "test case count"]:
    missing_before = int(clean_data[column].isna().sum())
    median_value = float(clean_data[column].median())
    clean_data[column] = clean_data[column].fillna(median_value)
    context_imputation[column] = (missing_before, median_value)

3. Feature Engineering and Analytical Datasets¶

In [8]:
phases = [
    "Test Planning",
    "Test Design",
    "Automation Development",
    "Test Execution",
    "Regression Testing",
    "Defect Management",
]

baseline_columns = [f"Baseline effort ({phase})" for phase in phases]
actual_columns = [f"Actual effort ({phase})" for phase in phases]

project_data = clean_data.copy()

for phase in phases:
    project_data[f"AI_{phase}"] = (
        project_data[f"AI Usage Testing Phase ({phase})"] == "Yes"
    ).astype(int)

project_data["AI_Phase_Count"] = project_data[
    [f"AI_{phase}" for phase in phases]
].sum(axis=1)
project_data["AI_Adoption_Rate"] = project_data["AI_Phase_Count"] / len(phases)

project_data["Total_Baseline_Effort"] = project_data[baseline_columns].sum(
    axis=1, min_count=len(phases)
)
project_data["Total_Actual_Effort"] = project_data[actual_columns].sum(
    axis=1, min_count=len(phases)
)
project_data["Total_Effort_Saved"] = (
    project_data["Total_Baseline_Effort"] - project_data["Total_Actual_Effort"]
)
project_data["Overall_Productivity_Improvement_Pct"] = (
    project_data["Total_Effort_Saved"]
    / project_data["Total_Baseline_Effort"]
    * 100
)
project_data["Story_to_Test_Ratio"] = (
    project_data["test case count"] / (project_data["User story count"] + 1)
)

phase_records = []
for row_id, row in project_data.iterrows():
    for phase in phases:
        phase_records.append({
            "Row_ID": row_id,
            "Sprint #": row["Sprint #"],
            "Year": row["Year"],
            "Sprint_Number": row["Sprint_Number"],
            "Application_Name": row["Application_Name"],
            "Team_Name": row["Team_Name"],
            "Complexity": row["Complexity"],
            "User story count": row["User story count"],
            "test case count": row["test case count"],
            "QE_Phase": phase,
            "AI_Used": row[f"AI Usage Testing Phase ({phase})"],
            "Baseline_Effort": row[f"Baseline effort ({phase})"],
            "Actual_Effort": row[f"Actual effort ({phase})"],
        })

phase_data = pd.DataFrame(phase_records)
phase_data["AI_Used_Flag"] = (phase_data["AI_Used"] == "Yes").astype(int)
phase_data["Effort_Saved"] = (
    phase_data["Baseline_Effort"] - phase_data["Actual_Effort"]
)
phase_data["Productivity_Improvement_Pct"] = np.where(
    phase_data["Baseline_Effort"] > 0,
    phase_data["Effort_Saved"] / phase_data["Baseline_Effort"] * 100,
    np.nan,
)
phase_data["Actual_to_Baseline_Ratio"] = np.where(
    phase_data["Baseline_Effort"] > 0,
    phase_data["Actual_Effort"] / phase_data["Baseline_Effort"],
    np.nan,
)
phase_data["Story_to_Test_Ratio"] = (
    phase_data["test case count"] / (phase_data["User story count"] + 1)
)
phase_data["Baseline_Effort_per_Story"] = (
    phase_data["Baseline_Effort"] / (phase_data["User story count"] + 1)
)

phase_valid = phase_data.dropna(
    subset=["Baseline_Effort", "Actual_Effort", "Productivity_Improvement_Pct"]
).copy()

analysis_inventory = pd.DataFrame({
    "Measure": [
        "Clean project/sprint observations",
        "Potential phase observations",
        "Valid phase productivity observations",
        "AI-assisted valid phase observations",
        "Traditional valid phase observations",
        "Applications after standardisation",
        "Teams after standardisation",
    ],
    "Value": [
        len(project_data),
        len(phase_data),
        len(phase_valid),
        int((phase_valid["AI_Used"] == "Yes").sum()),
        int((phase_valid["AI_Used"] == "No").sum()),
        project_data["Application_Name"].nunique(),
        project_data["Team_Name"].nunique(),
    ],
})
display(analysis_inventory)
analysis_inventory.to_csv(TABLES_DIR / "Analytical_Dataset_Inventory.csv", index=False)

project_data.to_csv(
    PROCESSED_DIR / "EQEPD_Cleaned_Project_Level.csv", index=False
)
phase_data.to_csv(
    PROCESSED_DIR / "EQEPD_Engineered_Phase_Level.csv", index=False
)

5. Preliminary Statistical Results¶

RQ1: AI-Assisted Versus Traditional Productivity¶

Because the distributions are non-normal and group variances differ, the Mann-Whitney U test is used as the primary inferential test. Welch's t-test is retained as a robustness comparison. Cohen's d and rank-biserial correlation provide practical-effect measures.

In [20]:
levene_result = stats.levene(ai_values, traditional_values, center="median")
welch_result = stats.ttest_ind(
    ai_values, traditional_values, equal_var=False
)
mann_whitney_result = stats.mannwhitneyu(
    ai_values, traditional_values, alternative="two-sided"
)

def cohens_d(group_1, group_2):
    n1, n2 = len(group_1), len(group_2)
    variance_1 = group_1.var(ddof=1)
    variance_2 = group_2.var(ddof=1)
    pooled_sd = math.sqrt(
        ((n1 - 1) * variance_1 + (n2 - 1) * variance_2)
        / (n1 + n2 - 2)
    )
    return (group_1.mean() - group_2.mean()) / pooled_sd

cohen_d = cohens_d(ai_values, traditional_values)
rank_biserial = (
    2 * mann_whitney_result.statistic
    / (len(ai_values) * len(traditional_values))
    - 1
)

rq1_results = pd.DataFrame({
    "Measure": [
        "AI mean productivity improvement (%)",
        "Traditional mean productivity improvement (%)",
        "Difference in means (percentage points)",
        "Levene p-value",
        "Welch t-test statistic",
        "Welch t-test p-value",
        "Mann-Whitney U statistic",
        "Mann-Whitney p-value",
        "Cohen's d",
        "Rank-biserial correlation",
    ],
    "Result": [
        ai_values.mean(),
        traditional_values.mean(),
        ai_values.mean() - traditional_values.mean(),
        levene_result.pvalue,
        welch_result.statistic,
        welch_result.pvalue,
        mann_whitney_result.statistic,
        mann_whitney_result.pvalue,
        cohen_d,
        rank_biserial,
    ],
})
display(rq1_results)
rq1_results.to_csv(TABLES_DIR / "RQ1_Preliminary_Results.csv", index=False)

RQ2: Differences Across QE Lifecycle Phases¶

The Kruskal-Wallis test assesses whether the distribution of productivity improvement differs across the six AI-assisted phase groups. Pairwise Mann-Whitney tests use Holm adjustment to control family-wise error.

In [21]:
ai_only = phase_valid[phase_valid["AI_Used"] == "Yes"].copy()

phase_groups = [
    ai_only.loc[
        ai_only["QE_Phase"] == phase,
        "Productivity_Improvement_Pct",
    ].values
    for phase in phases
]

kruskal_result = stats.kruskal(*phase_groups)
epsilon_squared = (
    kruskal_result.statistic - len(phases) + 1
) / (len(ai_only) - len(phases))

rq2_overall = pd.DataFrame({
    "Test": ["Kruskal-Wallis H", "p-value", "Epsilon-squared"],
    "Result": [
        kruskal_result.statistic,
        kruskal_result.pvalue,
        epsilon_squared,
    ],
})
display(rq2_overall)
rq2_overall.to_csv(TABLES_DIR / "RQ2_Overall_Test.csv", index=False)

pairwise_results = []
for phase_a, phase_b in combinations(phases, 2):
    values_a = ai_only.loc[
        ai_only["QE_Phase"] == phase_a,
        "Productivity_Improvement_Pct",
    ]
    values_b = ai_only.loc[
        ai_only["QE_Phase"] == phase_b,
        "Productivity_Improvement_Pct",
    ]
    test_result = stats.mannwhitneyu(
        values_a, values_b, alternative="two-sided"
    )
    effect_size = (
        2 * test_result.statistic / (len(values_a) * len(values_b)) - 1
    )
    pairwise_results.append({
        "Phase_A": phase_a,
        "Phase_B": phase_b,
        "Raw_p_value": test_result.pvalue,
        "Rank_Biserial": effect_size,
    })

pairwise_results = pd.DataFrame(pairwise_results)
pairwise_results["Holm_Adjusted_p"] = multipletests(
    pairwise_results["Raw_p_value"], method="holm"
)[1]
pairwise_results["Significant_at_0.05"] = (
    pairwise_results["Holm_Adjusted_p"] < 0.05
)

pairwise_results = pairwise_results.sort_values(
    "Holm_Adjusted_p"
).reset_index(drop=True)
display(pairwise_results)
pairwise_results.to_csv(
    TABLES_DIR / "RQ2_Phase_PostHoc_Results.csv", index=False
)

RQ3: Preliminary Influence Model¶

A multiple linear regression is estimated on the phase-level dataset. The target is winsorised at the 1st and 99th percentiles to reduce extreme leverage, and standard errors are clustered by sprint. Coefficients remain associations rather than causal effects.

In [22]:
regression_data = phase_valid.copy()
lower_clip, upper_clip = regression_data[
    "Productivity_Improvement_Pct"
].quantile([0.01, 0.99])

regression_data["Productivity_Winsorized"] = regression_data[
    "Productivity_Improvement_Pct"
].clip(lower_clip, upper_clip)

regression_data = regression_data.rename(columns={
    "Productivity_Winsorized": "Productivity",
    "AI_Used_Flag": "AI_Flag",
    "Baseline_Effort": "Baseline",
    "User story count": "User_Stories",
    "test case count": "Test_Cases",
    "QE_Phase": "Phase",
    "Application_Name": "Application",
})

regression_formula = (
    "Productivity ~ AI_Flag + Baseline + User_Stories + Test_Cases "
    "+ Year + Sprint_Number + C(Phase) + C(Complexity) + C(Application)"
)

influence_model = smf.ols(
    regression_formula, data=regression_data
).fit(
    cov_type="cluster",
    cov_kwds={"groups": regression_data["Sprint #"]},
)

coefficient_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Coefficient": influence_model.params,
    "p_value": influence_model.pvalues,
    "t_value": influence_model.tvalues,
    "CI_Lower": influence_model.conf_int()[0],
    "CI_Upper": influence_model.conf_int()[1],
})
coefficient_table["Absolute_t"] = coefficient_table["t_value"].abs()
coefficient_table = coefficient_table.sort_values(
    "Absolute_t", ascending=False
)

display(coefficient_table.head(15))
coefficient_table.to_csv(TABLES_DIR / "RQ3_Regression_Coefficients.csv")
(TABLES_DIR / "RQ3_Regression_Summary.txt").write_text(
    influence_model.summary().as_text(),
    encoding="utf-8",
)

6. Preliminary Predictive Modelling¶

In [23]:
model_data = project_data.dropna(
    subset=["Overall_Productivity_Improvement_Pct"]
).copy()

target_lower, target_upper = model_data[
    "Overall_Productivity_Improvement_Pct"
].quantile([0.01, 0.99])
model_data["Target_Productivity"] = model_data[
    "Overall_Productivity_Improvement_Pct"
].clip(target_lower, target_upper)

for phase in phases:
    baseline_column = f"Baseline effort ({phase})"
    model_data[f"Baseline_Share_{phase}"] = (
        model_data[baseline_column] / model_data["Total_Baseline_Effort"]
    )
    model_data[f"AI_Exposure_{phase}"] = (
        model_data[f"AI_{phase}"]
        * model_data[f"Baseline_Share_{phase}"]
    )

feature_columns = [
    "Application_Name",
    "Complexity",
    "Year",
    "Sprint_Number",
    "User story count",
    "test case count",
    "Story_to_Test_Ratio",
    "AI_Phase_Count",
    "Total_Baseline_Effort",
] + baseline_columns + [
    f"AI_{phase}" for phase in phases
] + [
    f"Baseline_Share_{phase}" for phase in phases
] + [
    f"AI_Exposure_{phase}" for phase in phases
]

X = model_data[feature_columns]
y = model_data["Target_Productivity"]
groups = model_data["Sprint #"]

group_split = GroupShuffleSplit(
    n_splits=1, test_size=0.20, random_state=42
)
train_index, test_index = next(
    group_split.split(X, y, groups=groups)
)

X_train = X.iloc[train_index]
X_test = X.iloc[test_index]
y_train = y.iloc[train_index]
y_test = y.iloc[test_index]

categorical_features = [
    column for column in feature_columns
    if X[column].dtype == "object"
]
numerical_features = [
    column for column in feature_columns
    if column not in categorical_features
]

split_summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Measure": [
        "Modelling records",
        "Training records",

        "Training sprints",
        "Testing sprints",
        "Sprint overlap",

        groups.iloc[test_index].nunique(),
        len(
            set(groups.iloc[train_index].unique()).intersection(
                set(groups.iloc[test_index].unique())

preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        (
            "numeric",
            Pipeline(steps=[
                ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
                ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
            ]),
            numerical_features,
        ),
        (
            "categorical",
            Pipeline(steps=[
                ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
                ("encoder", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),
            ]),
            categorical_features,
        ),
    ]
)

models = {
    "Linear Regression": LinearRegression(),
    "Random Forest": RandomForestRegressor(
        n_estimators=400,
        max_depth=10,
        min_samples_leaf=2,
        max_features=0.8,
        random_state=42,
        n_jobs=1,
    ),
    "Gradient Boosting": GradientBoostingRegressor(
        n_estimators=350,
        learning_rate=0.03,
        max_depth=2,
        min_samples_leaf=3,
        subsample=0.9,
        random_state=42,
    ),
}

model_results = []
fitted_models = {}
test_predictions = {}

for model_name, estimator in models.items():
    pipeline = Pipeline(steps=[
        ("preprocessor", preprocessor),
        ("model", estimator),
    ])
    pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
    predictions = pipeline.predict(X_test)

    model_results.append({
        "Model": model_name,
        "MAE": mean_absolute_error(y_test, predictions),
        "RMSE": math.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, predictions)),
        "R2": r2_score(y_test, predictions),
    })
    fitted_models[model_name] = pipeline
    test_predictions[model_name] = predictions

model_results = (
    pd.DataFrame(model_results)
    .sort_values("R2", ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
display(model_results)
model_results.to_csv(TABLES_DIR / "Preliminary_Model_Comparison.csv", index=False)

7. Interim Findings and Remaining Work¶

Preliminary findings¶

  • AI-assisted phase observations show substantially higher mean productivity improvement than traditional observations.
  • The RQ1 difference is statistically significant and practically large.
  • AI-derived value is phase-dependent rather than uniform.
  • Regression Testing, Test Design, and Automation Development are the strongest preliminary priority areas.
  • Random Forest provides the strongest grouped holdout performance, but the moderate R² means predictions should supplement managerial judgement.
  • The evidence supports targeted adoption and controlled governance rather than blanket deployment.

Remaining work for the final report¶

  • Complete sensitivity and robustness checks.
  • Review feature-importance stability across validation folds.
  • Finalise the business adoption roadmap and governance recommendations.
  • Add direct cost, quality, coverage, AI tool, and human-review variables when available.
  • Publish the repository and insert the active GitHub URL into the report.
